title: The y-intercept in context
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No existing point teaches interpreting the y-intercept as a starting amount or fixed cost in context; linear functions and cubic graphs only touch on it, and modelling with functions is a broader Year 12 idea.

draft.title: The y-intercept in context
card: The y-intercept is the value of y when x is zero. On a graph, it is the point where the line crosses the vertical axis.
In a real situation, it is the starting amount, before anything has changed. Often it is a fixed cost, such as a call-out fee, which is paid even if the job takes no time.
To find it from a table, look for the row where x = 0. If there is no such row, work backwards using the rate of change.
Example: a plumber charges $60 to arrive, then $40 for each hour of work. When hours = 0, the cost is $60. So the y-intercept is $60, the call-out fee.
draft.remember: The y-intercept is the value of y when x is zero: the starting amount.

a.q: A tutor's cost C (in dollars) for h hours is shown on a graph. The line crosses the vertical axis at C = 25. What does this 25 mean?
opts: The fixed fee charged before any hours are worked
The extra cost for each hour of tutoring
The number of hours that cost nothing
The cost of tutoring for 25 hours
a.why: The line crosses the axis where h = 0, so 25 is the cost with no hours worked. That is a fixed fee. The cost for each extra hour is the gradient, not the y-intercept.
a.clue: What is the number of hours at the point where the line meets the vertical axis?

b.q: Jaya hires a bike. The table shows the total cost, $C, for h hours: h = 1 gives $18, h = 2 gives $26, h = 3 gives $34. What is the y-intercept, and what does it mean?
b.why: The cost rises by $8 each hour, so one hour earlier the cost was $18 − $8 = $10. At h = 0 the cost is $10, which is the fixed fee. The $8 is the rate of change per hour, so it is the gradient.
b.clue: Work backwards one hour from h = 1 using the rise in cost.

a.best: The fixed fee charged before any hours are worked
